analysis:
Both changed files are test-only (scripts/test-provider-release-pipeline.py and scripts/test-provider-release-resolution.py); no runtime provider, coordinator, attestation or crypto code is modified. The tests pin a release-policy change. Master push now publishes staging only. Dev publication requires a push to the dev branch (release-dev-branch.yml), stamped -dev.branch.N. A dispatched dev lane is validation-only (publish=false). Prod stays tag-gated.

The tests tighten release-signing safeguards. They assert that prod cannot be reached from a branch push, that dev and staging pushes fail closed on the wrong environment or branch, and that the version override is ignored on push. They also assert that production secrets require the resolved prod environment, that the caller holds no secrets, and that the master resolver runs before candidate code.

A new test (head lines 316-343) asserts the final app meets the self-updater designated requirement, comparing the shell APP_REQUIREMENT to DarkbloomCodeSignature.swift byte for byte. This strengthens the T-013/T-034 update and signing-identity chain (A-011). No assertion removed weakens a control.

One removed base test asserted the dev concurrency group 'release-dev'. The new tests assert that no master path holds the group, which is consistent with the new design.

Unverified: the actual workflow files (release-swift.yml, release-provider.yml, release-dev-branch.yml) and scripts/resolve-provider-release.sh are not in this batch. I cannot confirm that they implement what the tests assert, or that release-dev-branch.yml, which now publishes dev, enforces the same trust gates (the verify-source env handling of a dev push, secret scoping). Integration should check those files. This is a coverage limit, not a finding.
